improvements.effect_range: Bounded by the expression/NUMERIC/DB_VALUE band that dominates both profiles. CUBRID spends 62.35% of profiled self cost there while retiring 2.949x the instructions per row at 1.073x better IPC, so this band carries the majority of the 2.74x total-query-CPU gap. A deferred-carry accumulator cannot remove the scan/deform cost, so the realistic ceiling is a large fraction of the aggregate band, not of the whole query.
improvements.evidence_event: heap rows scanned = 59,986,052 (identical both engines); denominator = total_query_cpu core-seconds per row, and retired instructions per row
improvements.explanation: PostgreSQL accumulates SUM/AVG into a 32-bit digit array with separate positive/negative buffers and propagates carry only once every NBASE-1 values, so the per-row cost is an int32 add per digit with no allocation, no precision recomputation and no rounding; CUBRID calls the general NUMERIC operator per row per aggregate, which memsets three VLA word buffers, converts both operands byte<->word, recomputes decimal precision, checks overflow, rounds/packs and builds a DB_VALUE.
improvements.implementation_direction: Introduce an aggregate-local fixed-point sum accumulator for NUMERIC SUM/AVG that defers carry propagation and precision/overflow normalization to finalization, keeping the general operator only for the final materialization; avoid per-row DB_VALUE construction inside qdata_evaluate_aggregate_list.

improvements.difficulty_reason: A scan-resistant replacement policy is a structural change to victim selection and zone promotion in page_buffer.c plus plumbing scan-context awareness from the executor to the buffer manager. Q04 adds that the random-probe case needs a different signal from the sequential-scan case, so a single BAS_BULKREAD-style ring is not a complete answer.
improvements.effect_range: Q01/Q03 bounded this as UPPER BOUND < 1% of CUBRID query CPU under WARM. Q04 replaces that bound with a DIRECT measurement: 1.160 core-s (12.13% of CUBRID's 9.565 core-s) is spent in the kernel page-cache read/copy path reached only through pgbuf_fix_release's miss branch, against 0.000 core-s on PostgreSQL, which takes zero physical reads for the same query at the same 8192MB budget. That is 25.5% of the 4.558 core-s CPU excess. It is an upper bound on what perfect retention would recover and a lower bound on the cost of non-retention, because the buffer-manager band (11.33%, 1.084 core-s) also contains victim-selection work that perfect retention would shrink but not eliminate.

improvements.explanation: CUBRID trace reports fetch=682,982 and ioread=682,950 for the lineitem scan, i.e. essentially every page fetch missed the 8192MB buffer, because the 682,937-page (10.42 GiB) heap exceeds the 524,288-page pool and plain LRU evicts pages before reuse; PostgreSQL under the same equal 8192MB budget kept 694,494 of 1,125,128 blocks resident (61.7% hit) because the bulk-read ring protects the resident set from scan-driven eviction.
improvements.implementation_direction: Unchanged in direction, widened in scope: a scan-resistant / access-aware replacement policy so a working set at 1.0-1.1x the pool retains a resident fraction instead of self-evicting. Q04 shows the target is not only large sequential scans but also random index-driven probes whose page set marginally exceeds the pool. A cheap first probe that would isolate policy from page size: re-run Q04 with data_buffer_size raised just past the projected 8510 MiB heap working set and confirm ioread collapses toward 0 - that is a diagnostic measurement, not a contract change, and must never be done inside a headline block.

why_the_working_set_differs.page_size_mechanism: CUBRID's 16 KiB page holds 87.8 lineitem rows against PostgreSQL's 53.3 in an 8 KiB page. For a sequential scan that is neutral, but for the random, order-clustered access Q04 performs it is not: the same selected row set spans 6.00 GiB of 16 KiB pages versus 3.62 GiB of 8 KiB pages, 1.66x more bytes for the same tuples. Page size is a storage-format constant, not a replacement-policy defect, so it is recorded as a CONTRIBUTING mechanism and the candidate remains about retention.

q04_random_access_at_identical_budget.why_this_is_the_cleanest_evidence: Q04 is the first query in the campaign where both engines run a STRUCTURALLY IDENTICAL plan (parallel full scan of orders + FK B-tree semi-join probe into lineitem with first-match exit) and issue a near-identical number of logical page fixes, so the reuse comparison is confounded neither by plan choice nor by work volume.

q06_rescoping.action_required: IMP-002's Q01, Q03 and Q04 evidence was all collected on parallel scans and has NOT been re-measured with the scan forced serial. Those relations are therefore FLAGGED FOR RE-VALIDATION: if a serial re-measurement of Q01/Q03/Q04 also lands on the predicted pool overflow, IMP-002's Q01/Q03/Q04 content belongs to IMP-010 and IMP-002 should be narrowed to its Q05 pool-hysteresis failure mode. This is recorded rather than acted on because re-measuring a closed query is outside Q06's scope and would need its own gated blocks.
q06_rescoping.parallel_case: The identical scan on 3/6/12 pooled workers retains only 213,957-224,728 pages and reads 468,980/458,209/459,242. The failure is real and large but is a property of the PARALLEL SCAN PATH, and is now tracked as IMP-010 with a source-localized cause (px_scan_task.cpp:94 does not propagate the session's private_lru_index, so pgbuf_unlatch_void_zone_bcb at page_buffer.c:6934 inserts into the middle of a shared list instead of the top of a private one).
q06_rescoping.q05_hysteresis_check: Q06's own block-to-block level wobble is 3.08% (medians 3.768-3.887 s over six gated blocks, non-monotone), consistent with Q05's history-dependent-equilibrium finding but an order of magnitude milder, and it tracks the level the preceding 40-statement warm left behind rather than drifting in one direction.
q06_rescoping.q06_steady_state_cost: Q06 adds no NEW steady-state cost evidence to IMP-002 beyond what IMP-010 now owns.
q06_rescoping.serial_control: One scan thread over a relation that exceeds the pool by 30.2% (682,937 pages vs 524,288) retains 524,007 pages and reads 158,930 - the arithmetically unavoidable overflow of 158,649 to within 0.18%. On the serial path the replacement policy is therefore not merely adequate, it is optimal, which directly contradicts 'replacement fails to retain a working set that marginally exceeds the pool' as a property of the POLICY.
q06_rescoping.summary: Q06 supplies the SERIAL CONTROL this candidate never had, and it does not support the current root-cause wording.

improvements.q08_relation: Q08 adds the strongest quantification so far and a projection that reaches parity. Five WARM-converged, load-gated CUBRID blocks give r(rchar,CPU) = +0.9779, r(CPU,wall) = +0.9717, an OLS slope of 0.4099 core-s per GiB of pool re-read and an intercept of 0.9752 s at zero churn, against PostgreSQL's measured 1.022423 s - i.e. absent the churn CUBRID would win Q08. Instability evidence: the identical warm statement measured 166 to 71,654 read syscalls across six forms on the same server (q8-iobisect.txt), so the miss count is a function of what the previous statement left resident, not of the statement. read_bytes = 0 on three of five blocks, so the cost is page-cache re-read CPU and not storage I/O. Working-set arithmetic for Q08's random index-driven pattern puts CUBRID at about 7.85 GiB of an 8.00 GiB pool (98% fill: 304,600 distinct lineitem pages + 151,689 orders pages at 16 KiB, plus part 380 MiB and customer 329 MiB) against PostgreSQL's about 2.65 GiB random footprint on 8 KiB pages with shared hit=796312 read=0 - the 'marginally exceeds the pool' condition this candidate names, on a random pattern like Q04's.
improvements.q09_evidence: Q09: CUBRID re-reads 30.497 GB per statement (1,861,608 x 16 KiB preads, read_bytes=0) at the contracted 8192 MB pool, PostgreSQL 18.647 GB. Present but explicitly REJECTED as Q09's deciding factor: with the pool held constant, CUBRID's own /*+ USE_HASH(orders, supplier) */ plan moves 23.61 GB/statement and finishes 1.5425x sooner, and PostgreSQL's forced index-NL plan moves 26.84 GB against its native 19.69 GB. The traffic is a property of the plan shape, not of the buffer budget. raw/Q09/Q09-cubrid-buffer-io-diag.json, raw/Q09/Q09-postgresql-buffer-io-diag.json.

q_evidence.Q11: Q11 bounds IMP-002's effect FROM ABOVE and separates it from IMP-018. Q11's entire referenced working set is ~97,400 pages of a 524,288-page pool (18.6%), so IMP-002's 'working set marginally exceeds the pool' premise is absent - and yet CUBRID takes 566,103 physical page reads per statement on the first connection and 0 in the saturated state, for the same plan and the same 1,012,000 page fixes. That is 2.6408x of Q11's wall (3.544 s -> 1.342 s) attributable to non-retention with the pool-size explanation excluded by construction. The mechanism is IMP-018's 5,000-page private-LRU ceiling, which is why a new ID was allocated; Q11 is recorded here because it is the strongest measurement of the SYMPTOM this candidate names, and because it refutes Q05's 'equilibrium it cannot leave without a server restart' - 20 further connections leave it with no restart (Num_data_page_lru1 15,092 -> 97,369).
q_evidence.Q12: Q12 is a genuine instance of this candidate's original premise -- a working set that exceeds the pool -- and it shows the SERIAL path is not optimal here, unlike Q06. CUBRID's referenced set is lineitem 682,937 pages + orders heap 151,689 pages + the orders PK index against a 524,288-page pool, so the arithmetically unavoidable overflow is at least 310,338 pages; the serial control measured 418,246 reads per statement, i.e. 1.35x the floor, against Q06's serial result of 158,930 versus a 158,649 floor (1.0018x). The difference is that Q12 interleaves 310,803 random index probes with the sequential scan, so the pure-sequential retention behaviour Q06 certified does not carry over. PostgreSQL at the identical 8192 MB budget reads 533,950 of 1,125,128 lineitem blocks and 0 of orders. No new effect size is claimed for IMP-002 from Q12: the addressable CPU is the same band IMP-010 and IMP-007 already bound at +0.5360 core-s, and attributing it three times would double-count. raw/Q12/q12-serial-io-serial-*.txt, q12-plan-act-pg.out, preflight-Q12.txt.
q_evidence.Q15: Q15 supplies this candidate's largest absolute figure so far, on a query where BOTH engines hold the same configured 8192 MB budget and BOTH take ZERO device reads (fully WARM, page-cache served). Per logical Q15 session CUBRID fetches 1,388,220 data pages (2 x 694,110, one per revenue0 expansion) and MISSES 1,116,942 of them - an 80.46% miss rate - against PostgreSQL's 268,652 of 2,250,257, i.e. 11.94%. The replacement search itself is the single largest symbol in CUBRID's profile: pgbuf_get_victim_candidates_from_lru at 10.19% = 3.994 core-s per session. A co-cause is quantified and kept separate rather than folded in: the same 59,986,052 lineitem rows occupy 682,937 x 16 KiB = 10,670.9 MiB on CUBRID against 1,125,128 x 8 KiB = 8,790.1 MiB on PostgreSQL (1.214x, 186.5 vs 153.6 bytes/row), which by itself drops resident coverage from 93.20% to 76.77% under the equal budget. Raw: q15-trace-cubrid.out (fetch/ioread), Q15-postgresql-headline-block1.json buffer_counters, q15-bands.txt, preflight-Q15.txt stored-size block. Evidence type: profile attribution.

improvements.evidence_event: LIKE evaluations per part scan: 2,000,000 actual vs 39,575 achievable; denominator = rows scanned in the part node (2,000,000). Selectivity: estimated 0.00921158 vs measured 399,587/2,000,000 = 0.19979.
improvements.explanation: CUBRID under-estimates leading-wildcard LIKE selectivity by 21.7x because it probes only bucket boundary values, and that wrong number, not any cost consideration, decides which conjunct runs first.
improvements.implementation_direction: In histogram_get_like_selectivity(), treat a pattern with no usable fixed prefix as not estimable from bucket boundaries: either probe per-bucket stored sample values, or set *success = false so qo_like_selectivity() falls back to PRM_ID_LIKE_TERM_SELECTIVITY. Separately and optionally, promote rank above selectivity in make_pred_from_bitset() when rank classes differ by more than one group.
improvements.mechanism_cubrid: For the non-MCV mass of a string histogram the estimator LIKE-tests one representative value per bucket - the bucket upper boundary bucket_hi - and, once the histogram has >=100 entries, uses that matching-bucket fraction directly as the selectivity. A bucket boundary is an artefact of sort order, so a suffix pattern uncorrelated with that order matches boundaries at a rate unrelated to its true frequency. The resulting selectivity flows into make_pred_from_bitset(), which orders AND-predicates by selectivity and consults its own heavy/light rank ONLY when two selectivities are exactly equal; so p_type like '%BRASS' (est 0.00921158, actual 0.19979) is placed ahead of p_size = 15 (est 0.02, actual 0.0198) and runs on all 2,000,000 part rows.
improvements.mechanism_postgresql: histogram_selectivity() applies the operator function across the histogram bound array and mcv_selectivity() across the MCV list, and patternsel combines both, so a leading-wildcard pattern is still estimated from values that actually occur: 0.26099 vs a true 0.19979 (1.31x). PostgreSQL's order_qual_clauses() then orders quals strictly by cost_qual_eval_node() per-tuple cost - though for this query textlike carries the same default procost as int4eq, so PostgreSQL ALSO evaluates the LIKE first; it is simply not hurt by it.

The Q16 instance costs no wall time -- the subquery is a 1,281-page scan either way and CUBRID's plan is unchanged -- so it is recorded as mechanism evidence, not as an effect. PostgreSQL's estimate on the identical predicate is 'rows=6' per worker (~30 total) against the same true 56, i.e. also low but by 1.9x rather than 5.6x, and it reaches that number through mcv_selectivity() + histogram_selectivity() applying the real operator (selfuncs.c:1032, :1042).

(c) It has direct upstream precedent (CBRD-27039) while IMP-004 has none.

improvements.correctness_risk: Medium-to-high. This path implements LIKE semantics for every collation, including contraction and UCA-level collations (lang_strmatch_utf8_w_contr, lang_strmatch_utf8_uca_w_level) and case-insensitive collations. The fast path must be gated so any non-deterministic collation, contraction table, case-insensitive collation, trailing-space rule or non-ASCII byte falls back to the existing loop.

improvements.effect_range: 8.64x-9.75x reduction of per-row LIKE cost. Upper bound on Q02 is the 46.72% band (0.836 of 1.79 core-s). Two independent methods bracket the same effect: 9.75x from profile self-time band, 8.64x from a same-engine A/B wall increment at equal active-unit counts. NOT additive with IMP-003.
improvements.evidence_event: CPU-seconds per part row for the LIKE predicate; denominator = 2,000,000 rows scanned in the part node. Profile band 46.72% x 1.79 core-s = 0.836 core-s -> 418.1 ns/row; PostgreSQL UTF8_MatchText 3.00% x 2.86 core-s = 0.0858 core-s -> 42.9 ns/row.
improvements.explanation: CUBRID pays codepoint decoding and collation-weight mapping per character for a predicate where byte equality would be sufficient, making its LIKE 8.64-9.75x more expensive per row than PostgreSQL's.
improvements.implementation_direction: Add an early fast path in lang_strmatch_utf8() (or dispatch from qstr_eval_like()) for deterministic built-in collations where both operands are ASCII: compare bytes directly and advance with an inlined continuation-byte skip, mirroring PostgreSQL's MatchText/NextChar. Secondarily make intl_utf8_to_cp and intl_nextchar_utf8 inlinable (static inline in a header, or hidden visibility) to remove the 2.82% PLT overhead.
measurement: Q13: LARGEST measurement of this candidate in the campaign. Profile band A = 33.01% of CUBRID's Q13 CPU = 15.995 core-s per statement, against PostgreSQL's UTF8_MatchText + textnlike at 12.57% = 2.773 core-s. Band ratio 5.5483x on the tight bracketing (matcher symbols only, both sides) and 4.2653x on the wide one (plus each engine's generic per-row expression dispatch); the band is 47.78% / 46.39% of Q13's entire 26.3964 core-s per-statement CPU gap under the two bracketings. Symbols: lang_strmatch_utf8 16.91, qstr_eval_like 7.40, intl_utf8_to_cp 3.53, intl_nextchar_utf8 1.77, intl_utf8_to_cp@plt 1.10, intl_nextchar_utf8@plt 0.63, db_string_like 0.41, eval_pred 1.26; 16.90 of the 16.91 points of lang_strmatch_utf8 sit under a single stack via eval_data_filter <- scan_next_index_lookup_heap. The predicate 'o_comment not like ''%special%requests%''' is evaluated 15,000,000 times per statement (trace btree rows: 15000000, lookup rows: 14837583, difference 162,417 = ground truth G2). TWO NEW SOURCE FACTS: (a) intl_utf8_to_cp@plt and intl_nextchar_utf8@plt appear as separate PLT symbols, proving the per-character decode is genuinely not inlined; (b) language_support.c:2843-2846 shows the only collation-dependent branch inside the matcher selects a different WEIGHT TABLE, never a different algorithm, so utf8_bin -- whose weight function is the identity -- still pays two intl_utf8_to_cp decodes (:2857,:2858) and two weight-table lookups (:2877,:2893) per character. CHARSET/COLLATION PARITY VERIFIED BEFORE ATTRIBUTION: PostgreSQL database tpch_sspq is encoding UTF8, so like.c:156-161 routes to UTF8_MatchText, NOT the SB_MatchText single-byte path; CUBRID's column is COLLATE utf8_bin. PostgreSQL's advantage is the UTF-8 specialization at like.c:128-134 (NextChar = pointer increment + continuation-byte test, no decode, no table, no call) plus the one-byte candidate rejection at like_match.c:174-185. RECOMMEND RAISING TO P0 at the next ledger review on this evidence.
improvements.mechanism_cubrid: lang_strmatch_utf8() advances one character at a time and per position calls intl_utf8_to_cp() on both the target and the pattern, then maps each resulting codepoint through the collation weight table before comparing. There is no ASCII fast path and no byte-lockstep comparison, so a pure-ASCII pattern against an ASCII column still pays two codepoint decodes plus two table lookups per character. The profile shows both decode helpers reached through the dynamic linker on every character: intl_utf8_to_cp 4.82% + @plt 1.75%, intl_nextchar_utf8 3.09% + @plt 1.07% - 2.82% of total query CPU is PLT stub overhead alone.
improvements.mechanism_postgresql: MatchText() documents and implements byte-by-byte comparison even for multi-byte encodings, on the grounds that text and pattern stay in lockstep outside wildcard handling, and advances characters with a two-instruction inline macro that just skips UTF-8 continuation bytes. No codepoint is materialized, no weight table is consulted, and there is no out-of-line call in the inner loop.

improvements.effect_range: Diagnosability only; zero measured runtime effect (query results and headline timings are unaffected). improvements.explanation: Under a parallel outer scan, CUBRID's query trace multiplies the reported work of nested-loop levels deeper than 2 by (depth-1), because two overlapping traversals both merge the same worker statistics.
improvements.implementation_direction: In px_scan_trace_handler.cpp:492-500, stop the double traversal. Either (a) merge only the node itself per level by extracting the single-node body of xasl_merge_stats into a merge_one_node() helper and calling that inside the scan_ptr loop, or (b) keep xasl_merge_stats' subtree semantics and drop the caller's scan_ptr loop, calling it once on xasl_tree->scan_ptr. Option (b) is the smaller diff; option (a) is clearer about intent. The dptr_list loop at :496-499 needs the same review, since dptr subtrees reached from a level that was already subtree-merged are duplicated by the same mechanism.
measurement:
Three independent scales, all with engine-independent ground truth:
(1) Q03 full scale, parallel outer scan (q3-trace-cubrid.out): lineitem index entries reported 11,691,206 vs true 5,845,603 (2.0000x) and heap lookups 604,228 vs true 302,114 (2.0000x, ground truth q3-groundtruth-cubrid.out and PostgreSQL's own 302,114 at q3-plan-act-pg.out); the orders level (depth 2) is exact at 1,461,923 on both engines.
(2) Small slice, SERIAL control (q3-doubling-trace.out, index outer scan so no parallel scan): every level exact - customer 1,079, orders 5,422, lineitem entries 21,847, lineitem qualifying 1,056, all equal to ground truth q3-doubling-groundtruth.out.
(3) Same slice with a PARALLEL outer scan forced by c_custkey-0<5000 (q3-doubling-parallel-trace.out): depth 2 still exact (readkeys 1,079, rows 11,054, lookups 5,422) while depth 3 is exactly 2x (readkeys 10,844, rows 43,694, lookups 2,112).
(4) Falsifiable prediction of the code reading, tested: a depth-4 chain must report 3x. Measured (q3-doubling-depth4-trace.out vs q3-doubling-depth4-groundtruth.out): depth-3 lineitem 17,810 vs true 8,905 (2.0000x) and depth-4 partsupp 26,715 vs true 8,905 (3.0000x).

(5) Q04 NEGATIVE CONTROL - no duplication, every counter exact under a 6-worker parallel outer scan:
orders scan readrows reported 15,000,000 vs true cardinality 15,000,000; correlated-subquery readkeys reported 573,671 vs true probe count 573,671 (q4-groundtruth-{cubrid,pg}.out, identical on both engines); lookup rows reported 526,040 vs true answer row count 526,040.
WHY: Q04's XASL hangs the correlated EXISTS subquery off the ROOT node's dptr_list and has NO scan_ptr chain (single-table driving scan, no nested-loop join). merge_xasl_tree() therefore merges it exactly once at src/query/parallel/px_scan/px_scan_trace_handler.cpp:467-470, and the duplicating loop at :493-500 never executes because xasl_tree->scan_ptr is nullptr.
WHAT THIS PINS: this is the negative control the Q03 entry asked for. It SCOPES the defect - the (depth-1) multiplication requires a non-empty scan_ptr chain, so a correlated subquery under the root is unaffected - and it pins the root-dptr merge path with exact numbers a fix must preserve. It does NOT clear the :496-499 inner dptr_list loop, which merges a dptr hanging off a scan_ptr LEVEL and is still double-counted by construction, because the outer xasl_merge_stats(xptr1) has already recursed into xptr1's dptr_list via iterate_xasl_tree (src/xasl/xasl_iteration.hpp:180-187, called from src/xasl/xasl_iteration.cpp:205); Q04 simply does not exercise it.

improvements.mechanism_cubrid: Each parallel worker executes a private clone of the sub-plan below the parallel scan. When a worker finishes, merge_xasl_tree() folds its XASL clone into the coordinator's tree. For the nested-loop chain it iterates the scan_ptr list and calls xasl_merge_stats(xptr1, main) for every level. xasl_merge_stats does not merge a single node: its last statement is iterate_xasl_tree(src, merge_stats, true), which recurses through scan_ptr (xasl_iteration.hpp:189-191) and merges every node in the subtree by header.id with +=. So the level-2 node is merged once (from the caller's first iteration), the level-3 node twice (once inside level-2's subtree walk, once from the caller's second iteration), the level-4 node three times, and a level-k node (k-1) times. The output row counts, and therefore query results, are unaffected - only the trace counters are.
improvements.mechanism_postgresql: PostgreSQL keeps a per-worker NodeInstrumentation array in DSM and merges it with planstate_tree_walker (execParallel.c:1173), which visits every PlanState exactly once; for the node being visited it loops over the worker slots and calls InstrAggNode once per worker (execParallel.c:1115). The merge primitive itself (instrument.c:232) touches only the node handed to it and never re-walks children, so no node can be visited by two overlapping traversals.

q06_evidence.defect_2_impact: A user reading a parallel Q06 trace cannot tell that 98.1% of the scanned rows were discarded by the sargs, which is precisely the number needed to judge whether an index would help. It is an observability defect with no runtime cost.
q06_evidence.defect_2_rows_counter: For the identical query and identical result, the serial trace reports the scan's output correctly as 'rows: 1139264' while every parallel trace reports 'rows: 59986052' - the READROWS value, i.e. the qualified-row counter is overwritten by the scanned-row counter on the parallel gather path. Evidence: variants/trace-NOPARALLELSCAN.txt and variants/trace-PARALLEL1.txt both show readrows 59986052 / rows 1139264; q6-trace-cubrid.out (6 workers), variants/trace-PARALLEL3.txt and variants/trace-PARALLEL12.txt all show readrows 59986052 / rows 59986052. Ground truth is 1,139,264, confirmed identically on both engines by count(*) (q6-groundtruth-cubrid.out, q6-groundtruth-pg.out) and by PostgreSQL's own actual plan (rows=189877.33 loops=6 = 1,139,264 with 'Rows Removed by Filter: 9807798' x 6 = 58,846,788; 1,139,264 + 58,846,788 = 59,986,052 exactly).
q06_evidence.defect_3_statdump_counters: The server-global page-buffer counters do not advance at all for the parallel scan path: cubrid statdump reported Num_data_page_fetches = 23,255,736, Num_data_page_ioreads = 814,716 and Data_page_buffer_hit_ratio = 96.49 both BEFORE and AFTER a statement that provably issued 608,635 pread syscalls totalling 9.29 GiB (/proc/<cub_server>/io syscr and rchar deltas, q6-cubrid-bufstate.txt). Two consecutive invocations returned byte-identical values including Num_data_page_hash_anchor_waits. All of Q06's buffer evidence therefore rests on the trace counters plus /proc/<pid>/io, and statdump's page gauges are recorded as UNRELIABLE for this campaign.
q06_evidence.original_defect_control: Q06's scan_ptr chain is depth 1, so the documented (k-1)x multiplication predicts an exact counter, and the trace's fetch (682,938) and ioread (608,427) match the independently measured page count (682,937 heap pages) and syscall count (608,496-608,635) to within 0.03%. Q06 is therefore a POSITIVE control that bounds the original defect to nested chains, complementing Q05's negative control which bounded it to chains that actually get parallel workers.
q06_evidence.summary: Q06 adds a SECOND, mechanically distinct parallel-scan statistics defect in the same subsystem, plus a positive control for the original one.

improvements.q17_evidence: Q17 is the third independent depth-3 instance and the FIRST to exercise the SUBQUERY_CACHE counters, which no prior query reached. Every counter under the correlated SUBQUERY node is reported at exactly 2x, verified against independently measured ground truth three separate times in the same session: SUBQUERY_CACHE miss 4,088 against 2,044 distinct qualifying p_partkey values; miss 8,102 against 4,051 (widened container predicate); miss 32,060 against 16,030 (p_container LIKE 'MED%'). The subquery's index-scan counters double identically -- readkeys 20,438 vs the outer scan's 10,219, filteredkeys 16,350 vs 8,175, rows 122,770 vs 61,385 -- so the true values are exactly half of what the trace prints. NEW CONSEQUENCE beyond the counter inflation already recorded: the traced cache `size` is inflated by the same merge, and is therefore not comparable to max_subquery_cache_size at all. Measured proof: three runs reported a size LARGER than the budget they ran under while still reporting status=enabled -- size 1,980,048 under a 2 MB budget, size 2,445,672 under 2 MB, size 5,224,800 under 2 MB, and size 1,539,408 under an explicit 1,500,000-byte budget. An operator reading the trace would conclude the cache was 94.4% full and about to be disabled by the subquery_cache.c:378-383 cliff when in fact it held 7.8x more keys without disabling. Observability only: no wall effect on Q17, so ranked FOURTH of Q17's relations, above IMP-019 only because it actively misleads capacity planning.

q_evidence.Q11: Q11 NEGATIVE CONTROL. Every CUBRID trace row counter on Q11 is EXACT against ground truth that both engines answer identically: partsupp SCAN `rows: 323920` == G3 323,920, supplier SCAN `rows: 4049` == G2 4,049, GROUPBY `rows: 8685` == G5 8,685, nation `readrows: 25` == 25. Q11's scan nest is depth 3 (nation -> supplier -> partsupp), the same depth at which Q08/Q10 saw 1.96x-2x inflation, so the defect is depth-INDEPENDENT in the way IMP-005 currently states it: Q11 runs no parallel scan units (U=1.00965, no `parallel workers` sub-line anywhere in the trace), and xasl_merge_stats' double-merge needs the parallel sibling-XASL path. Q11 therefore sharpens IMP-005: the inflation is a property of PARALLEL scan trace merging, not of nesting depth alone. Q11's F_work is safe to build from trace counters, and it is.
q_evidence.Q12: Q12 adds a second, larger instance of the same parallel-worker statistics defect and extends it from the trace to statdump. Trace side: for the native parallel plan the traced statement reports 'SELECT (fetch: 113)' and 'SCAN (table: dba.lineitem) ... fetch: 44, readrows: 0, rows: 0' on the main thread while statdump's Num_data_page_fetches bracketed around that same statement moves by 1,788,621 -- the SELECT node under-reports page fixes by 15,829x, and readrows is reported as 0 for a scan that read 59,986,052 rows (the per-worker range line '(parallel workers: 6, readrows: 9938887..10011920)' is the only place the real figure appears, and it is a RANGE, not a total). The same statement run with /*+ NO_PARALLEL_SCAN */ reports every field correctly: 'SELECT (fetch: 2608801, ioread: 417881)' matching its statdump delta of 2,608,803 to 2 fixes. Second, new observation: the 4-statement diagnostic block moved Num_data_page_fetches by exactly 0 (106,169,292 -> 106,169,292 across 24 statements) while the single traced statement moved it by 1,788,621, i.e. the server-wide page counters appear to accumulate only while statement-level tracing is active. That is recorded as an OBSERVATION with its evidence, not as a proven mechanism -- the likely gate is perfmon_is_perf_tracking_and_active(), but this campaign did not run the controlled experiment that would prove it, and the practical consequence is only that Q12 used the trace-bracketed statdump deltas and /proc/<cub_server>/io rather than the block-bracketed statdump. raw/Q12/q12-serial-parallel.out, q12-serial-serial.out, q12-serial-statdump-*.txt, Q12-cubrid-buffer-io-diag.json.
q_evidence.Q15: Q15 reproduces the parallel-path `rows = readrows` defect on BOTH revenue0 expansions: each SCAN (table: dba.lineitem) line reports readrows: 59986052, rows: 59986052 with `parallel workers: 6`, where the true post-filter count is 2,265,714 - a 26.5x overstatement of the rows the group-by actually receives. The operational consequence for this campaign is concrete and is why Q15 cites the defect at all: the section 16 F_work event could NOT be read from the trace and had to be established by independent count(*) ground truth on both engines (2,265,714 on each, with 100,000 distinct l_suppkey on each), which is the fourth query forced onto that workaround. Raw: q15-trace-cubrid.out, variants/q15-groundtruth.out, q15-plan-act-pg-warm.out. Evidence type: direct A/B.

improvements.ranking_rationale: Ranked below IMP-006 and IMP-007 on runtime effect, which is zero, and above nothing on that axis. It is recorded at P2 rather than P3 because it is a precondition for trusting the other two: Q03's own F_work would have been wrong by 1.54x on the native side if the trace had been believed. It is also the cheapest fix in the registry (a one-loop change) with the lowest risk.

alternative: drop the caller's scan_ptr loop instead of narrowing xasl_merge_stats - same outcome, smaller diff, slightly higher risk of under-counting dptr subtrees
relations.note: Independent of every other candidate: it changes reported numbers, not executed work. It does interact with all of them as an evidence-quality prerequisite.

improvements.root_cause_title: Parallel-scan trace statistics for a nested-loop subtree are merged once per scan_ptr level and again by the whole-subtree walk inside xasl_merge_stats, so a level-k scan's counters are reported (k-1) times: depth 3 is exactly 2x and depth 4 exactly 3x
improvements.upstream_precedent: Yes, same class: 85984d18d [CBRD-26839] 'Emit zero-stats parallel heap scan trace when no worker stats collected' (#7219), 2be90e6dd [CBRD-26704] 'Modify trace results to be hidden when Correlated subquery cache is not used' (#7043) and 34fc7779a [CBRD-26681] 'Exclude memoize trace results from output when Memoize is not used' (#7018) are all parallel-scan trace-output correctness fixes in the same subsystem, and all are ancestors of the pinned build. The defect itself was introduced by 0c6088ab3 [CBRD-26722] (#7062).
improvements.validation_criteria: (1) q3-doubling-parallel-trace.out reports depth-3 readkeys 5,422, rows 21,847, lookups 1,056 - byte-equal to the serial control q3-doubling-trace.out; (2) the depth-4 probe reports partsupp 8,905, not 26,715; (3) Q03's full trace reports lineitem entries 5,845,603 and lookups 302,114, matching PostgreSQL's 302,114; (4) MEMOIZE and SUBQUERY_CACHE hit/miss and the sq_cache totals are unchanged on the Q02 correlated-subquery trace, proving the dptr path was not broken; (5) no change to any query result or headline timing. (6) Q04 REGRESSION PIN, added from the Q04 negative control: after the fix, Q04's trace must still report orders readrows 15,000,000, subquery readkeys 573,671 and lookup rows 526,040 exactly, proving the root-dptr merge path (px_scan_trace_handler.cpp:467-470) was not broken while the scan_ptr double traversal was removed.

improvements.correctness_risk: High for the full change: list-file records carry the tuple format that sort, group-by, hash join, subquery cache and the client protocol all decode, and lifetime of a referenced tuple must outlive the parent's use of it, so a streaming mode risks use-after-free and format skew. The tuple-descriptor caching sub-step is low risk and independently testable.

improvements.difficulty_reason: List files are the universal currency between CUBRID's XASL nodes (sort, group-by, hash join build/probe, subquery caches, client fetch all consume QFILE_TUPLE records), so introducing a pass-by-reference tuple between adjacent pipelined operators is a structural executor change, not a localized early return.
improvements.effect_range: Upper bound on Q03's controlled plan is the 6.26 core-second band; the difference against PostgreSQL's comparable band is 5.23 core-seconds, i.e. 18.7% of the 28.04 core-second CPU excess at matched shape. No wall-clock claim is made for CUBRID's native plan, where this band is smaller because the native index-nested-loop plan materializes 10,766,102 tuple touches instead of 118,590,174. Evidence type: profile attribution on top of a direct plan A/B.
improvements.evidence_event: CPU-seconds in the intermediate-tuple materialization band per statement at matched plan shape; denominator = 118,590,174 plan-node tuple touches (CUBRID controlled) vs 118,818,354 (PostgreSQL), which agree to 0.19%
improvements.explanation: At an identical plan shape with identical per-node row counts, CUBRID needs 2.29x the instructions per tuple that PostgreSQL needs, and the largest single identifiable component is copying every intermediate tuple into a list-file record instead of passing a slot by reference.
improvements.implementation_direction: Introduce a pass-by-reference tuple between adjacent pipelined operators so that a list file is written only where a node must retain or re-read tuples (sort input, hash build, subquery cache, client fetch). Concretely: give BUILDLIST_PROC a streaming output mode that hands the parent a value-array view instead of calling qfile_generate_tuple_into_list (query_executor.c:1255), and let the hash-join probe (query_hash_join.c:4277) emit that view directly to its parent when the parent is a group-by that consumes tuples in order. Cheaper first step with the same direction: cache the tuple descriptor across tuples rather than rebuilding it per tuple in qdata_generate_tuple_desc_for_valptr_list (query_opfunc.c:625), which is 3.04% of profiled cost on its own.
improvements.measurement: Controlled same-shape A/B (the only way to compare per-tuple cost without plan confounding): CUBRID with /*+ USE_HASH */ reaches PostgreSQL's shape with identical counts at every node - customer 1,500,000 scanned / 300,276 built, orders 15,000,000 scanned / 7,289,442 probes / 1,461,923 matched, lineitem 59,986,052 scanned / 32,334,250 probes / 302,114 matched, 114,003 groups (q3-trace-cubrid-hash.out vs q3-plan-act-pg.out). At that shape: total_query_cpu 50.36 vs 22.32 core-seconds (F_cpu 2.2563), F_work 0.9981, F_cost 2.2606, 424.7 vs 187.8 ns per tuple touch. perf decomposes F_cost cleanly: instructions per tuple 2,274.3 vs 991.4 (2.294x) at essentially equal instruction throughput (5.3557e9 vs 5.2776e9 instructions per core-second, 1.015x; IPC 1.96 vs 1.95), so the deficit is instruction count, not stalling. Band: 12.43% x 50.36 = 6.26 core-seconds versus PostgreSQL's comparable spill band 5.36% x 19.28 = 1.03 core-seconds.
improvements.mechanism_cubrid: For each tuple crossing a node boundary CUBRID (a) calls fetch_val_list() to evaluate every regu variable into DB_VALUEs, (b) calls qdata_generate_tuple_desc_for_valptr_list() to rebuild a tuple descriptor, (c) computes each value's on-tuple size, (d) memcpy's each value into the list-file page via qdata_copy_db_value_to_tuple_value(), and (e) clears the DB_VALUEs. Every downstream node then re-reads and re-decodes that record. The Q03 controlled-plan profile shows the band as fetch_val_list 3.81% + qdata_generate_tuple_desc_for_valptr_list 3.04% + qdata_copy_db_value_to_tuple_value 2.84% + qfile_generate_tuple_into_list 1.51% + qdata_get_tuple_value_size_from_dbval 1.23% = 12.43%, with heap_attrinfo_read_dbvalues a further 10.52% feeding it.
improvements.mechanism_postgresql: ExecProcNode returns a pointer to the child's TupleTableSlot (executor.h:322). Attributes are deformed lazily and only as far as needed (execTuples.c:1017 slot_deform_heap_tuple, called from tts_buffer_heap_getsomeattrs at :751). A copy happens only where a node must retain the tuple: the hash table stores a MinimalTuple (nodeHash.c:1774/1779) and a spilling batch writes to a SharedTuplestore. Its top symbol is therefore the same *kind* of work (tts_buffer_heap_getsomeattrs 21.62% of the executor) but it is paid once per tuple per scan rather than once per pipeline edge.

The 5.23 core-second difference is 18.7% of the entire 28.04 core-second CPU excess that makes CUBRID 1.9410x slower than PostgreSQL on the same plan.
improvements.q10_evidence: Q10: the intermediate join result is materialised into a temp list file and then read back as a separate plan node - CUBRID's trace shows `SCAN (temp time: 805, fetch: 58572, ioread: 0, readrows: 1147084, rows: 1147084)` feeding the GROUPBY, i.e. 1,147,084 tuples written and 1,147,084 read back, 805 ms (10.0% of the 8048 ms traced statement) purely to hand rows from the join to the aggregation. PostgreSQL's equivalent hand-off is a TupleTableSlot passed by reference from the Nested Loop straight into the Sort, with no intermediate file. Profile band: 5.66% of CUBRID's cycles in list-file tuple materialisation (qdata_copy_db_value_to_tuple_value 1.13%, qdata_generate_tuple_desc_for_valptr_list 1.05%, qfile_locate_tuple_next_value 0.90%, qfile_locate_tuple_value_r 0.73%, qdata_get_tuple_value_size_from_dbval 0.59%, qfile_generate_tuple_into_list 0.47%, pr_data_writeval_disk_size 0.41%, qfile_save_tuple 0.38%). Independent corroboration that this cost is real and separable: the /*+ NO_HASH_AGGREGATE */ variant, which changes only the aggregation, drops the same node from 805 ms to 274 ms because the 5 parallel sort workers consume it concurrently.

q_evidence.Q11: Q11's SHARPEST measurement so far, and the largest remaining CUBRID-specific cost once IMP-018 is removed. In the saturated state CUBRID performs 1,011,949 data-page fixes per statement against PostgreSQL's 676,275 shared-buffer accesses for the same plan. CUBRID's join subtree, run twice, accounts for 340,127 + 340,131 = 680,258 of them - within 0.6% of PostgreSQL's ENTIRE total - so the remaining 331,691 fixes (32.8% of all CUBRID page fixes) are the aggregation's temp list-file write plus re-read and its sort pages. PostgreSQL's aggregation performs ZERO shared-buffer accesses: its HashAggregate spill is temp-file traffic (`temp read=1330 written=3103`) outside the buffer manager entirely. Since F_cpu(native) 1.358179x decomposes exactly as F_work 1.496357x (page fixes) x F_cost 0.907657x (CPU per fix), and CUBRID is CHEAPER per fix, essentially all of Q11's CPU gap is this fix count - of which 32.8% is this candidate. Profile band: qfile_generate_tuple_into_list 0.83 + qexec_end_one_iteration 0.78 + qdata_generate_tuple_desc_for_valptr_list 0.71 + qdata_copy_db_value_to_tuple_value 0.41 = 2.73% of self cost, which UNDERSTATES it, because the pgbuf fix work those 331,691 fixes cause is banded under pgbuf (21.07%), not here.

improvements.ranking_rationale: Ranked first among the Q03 candidates on measured share of the matched-shape CPU excess (18.7%, versus IMP-007's critical-path difference of 2.22 core-seconds = 7.9%) and first on generality: every multi-node plan in the workload pays it, whereas IMP-007 only bites when the working set exceeds the buffer pool. It is ranked below IMP-007 on cost-effectiveness, because IMP-007's first step is an advisory fadvise call with upstream precedent while this is a structural executor change - which is why the tuple-descriptor caching sub-step (3.04% of profiled cost on its own) is called out separately as the cheap first move. Not summed with IMP-007: they are disjoint bands of the same profile (qdata/qfile versus kernel page copy), verified disjoint by symbol.

improvements.root_cause_title: Every intermediate join result tuple is materialized into a list-file page through a per-value DB_VALUE -> tuple copy (tuple descriptor build, per-value size computation, memcpy, clear), where PostgreSQL passes a TupleTableSlot by reference and only materializes when a node genuinely must store the tuple
improvements.upstream_precedent: Partial. No prior commit removes an intermediate list-file materialization, but two ancestors of the pinned build reduce work on the same edge rather than the copy itself: 5795b1ab6 [CBRD-26900] 'Evaluate eligible after-join predicates in the hash join probe loop' (#7269) filters before the tuple is emitted, and cb2c79715 [CBRD-26648] 'Support partial aggregate with hash table' (#6949) avoids materializing group-by input. Recorded as no direct precedent for pass-by-reference pipelining.
improvements.validation_criteria: (1) Q03 controlled-plan (/*+ USE_HASH */) total_query_cpu below 40 core-seconds with byte-identical 10-row output versus sink/Q03-cubrid-hash-block.out; (2) the qdata/qfile band below 6% of profiled self cost in a re-profiled controlled run; (3) Q01-Q22 results byte-identical; (4) no regression in the native Q03 plan (median wall <= 4.808 s); (5) for the descriptor-caching sub-step alone, qdata_generate_tuple_desc_for_valptr_list below 0.5% with unchanged results.

improvements.correctness_risk: Low for (1): fadvise is advisory, the only risk being eviction of useful page-cache content. Medium for (2): multi-page reads must not cross volume or extent boundaries, must respect page validation and the double-write-buffer path (page_buffer.c:8454 dwb_read_page precedes fileio_read on the same miss path), and must not install pages a concurrent writer is modifying. High for (3), which introduces buffer states for in-flight reads that the buffer manager cannot currently represent.

improvements.difficulty_reason: Read combining for sequential scans is a bounded change at the pgbuf/fileio boundary, but genuine asynchronous I/O requires a submission/completion path and buffer states for in-flight reads, which the buffer manager currently has no representation for.
improvements.effect_range: 2.22 core-seconds of critical-path CPU at matched plan shape (7.9% of the 28.04 core-second excess) is the directly attributed difference; up to 3.96 of 21.91 core-seconds sits in the same band in the native plan, where it coincides with IPC falling to 0.94. This is an UPPER BOUND on what asynchrony could remove from the critical path, not a prediction of wall-clock gain: PostgreSQL's own accounting shows the work is moved rather than eliminated, and it spends 0.432 core-seconds per GiB read in total against CUBRID's 0.221, so a naive port of the io-worker design would increase total CPU.
improvements.evidence_event: CPU-seconds of kernel page-copy and page-cache-lookup work charged to executor threads per statement; denominator = bytes read from outside the buffer pool per statement (13.59 GiB CUBRID controlled, 8.10 GiB PostgreSQL, both from /proc/<pid>/io rchar)
improvements.explanation: CUBRID pays for every buffer miss with a blocking single-page read on the thread that needs the page, so page-cache copy time is serialized into query execution; PostgreSQL performs the equivalent work in io worker processes and keeps its executor free, which is worth 2.22 core-seconds of critical-path CPU at matched plan shape even though PostgreSQL spends more total CPU per byte.
improvements.implementation_direction: Ordered by evidence strength. (1) Per-scan readahead: issue posix_fadvise(POSIX_FADV_WILLNEED) for the next run of pages of a sequential or index-range scan, reusing the parameter machinery already present for the mount-time advise (file_io.c:3050) - this overlaps the kernel copy with executor work without any new buffer state, and has direct upstream precedent. (2) Batch the miss path: when the requesting scan is sequential, fetch a run of adjacent pages with the existing fileio_read_pages() (file_io.c:4211) in one call - justified by call-overhead reduction only, NOT by submission-count parity, which the measurement refutes. (3) Only if (1) and (2) prove insufficient, scope genuine asynchronous data-page I/O with in-flight buffer states; the measured total-CPU-per-byte comparison says this must be justified by critical-path latency, not by CPU savings.
improvements.measurement:
Matched plan shape (/*+ USE_HASH */ versus PostgreSQL native, identical per-node row counts).
Critical-path kernel I/O cost: CUBRID rep_movs_alternative 5.95% x 50.36 = 3.00 core-seconds inside cub_server's query threads (profile-cubrid-hash-flat.txt); PostgreSQL next_uptodate_folio 2.48% + rep_movs_alternative 1.58% = 4.06% x 19.28 = 0.78 core-seconds inside leader+workers (profile-pg-flat.txt), plus 2.72 core-seconds of pg_io_worker CPU recorded as auxiliary (Q03-postgresql-telemetry-run1.json). Difference on the critical path: 2.22 core-seconds = 7.9% of the 28.04 core-second excess.
Bytes and syscalls per statement (/proc/<pid>/io): CUBRID rchar 13,594,346,680 (12.66 GiB) in syscr 829,884 read calls = 17.2 KiB per call; PostgreSQL rchar 8,694,806,235 (8.10 GiB) in syscr 551,551 = 15.4 KiB per call. Device read_bytes ~0 on both sides (CUBRID 0.00 MiB, PostgreSQL 0.12 MiB), so this is page-cache copy and syscall cost, never disk latency.
Native CUBRID plan for context: 831,427 corrected page misses (IMP-005 correction applied; the corrected count x 16 KiB = 12.69 GiB matches the independently measured rchar of 13.09 GiB per statement to 3.3%, whereas the uncorrected trace count would imply 25.4 GiB, i.e. 1.92x more than the measured syscall bytes - which is what proves the correction), kernel band 18.07% x 21.91 = 3.96 core-seconds, and IPC collapses to 0.94 versus 1.96 at matched shape.
REJECTED sub-hypothesis, with the number that rejected it: 'CUBRID lacks read combining, so it issues far more I/O submissions than PostgreSQL at io_combine_limit=16.' The code fact is real (fileio_read reads exactly one page; fileio_read_pages is log-only), but the measurement refutes any submission-count penalty: CUBRID moves 17.2 KiB per read syscall versus PostgreSQL's 15.4 KiB, and PostgreSQL's 551,551 calls for ~900,213 block reads (746,768 heap + 153,445 temp) average only 1.63 blocks per call, not 16. Read combining is therefore NOT claimed as an effect here.

Q04 (structurally identical plans on both engines, no hint needed):
276,950 blocking pread() calls per statement at 16,377 bytes each - exactly one 16 KiB page per call, confirming the single-page read path - all issued from cub_server 'parallel-query' executor threads, against 415 read syscalls on PostgreSQL (667.3x). rchar 4,535,681,928 B/statement vs 1,390,736 B. The call graph resolves 10.18% of CUBRID's CPU to rep_movs_alternative reached ONLY via __libc_pread64 <- fileio_read <- pgbuf_claim_bcb_for_fix <- pgbuf_fix_release; with filemap_get_read_batch 1.26% and filemap_read 0.69% the band is 12.13% = 1.160 core-s against PostgreSQL's 0.000 core-s.
SCOPE NOTE: on Q04 the io-worker contrast that motivated this candidate on Q03 does NOT apply, because PostgreSQL performs zero physical reads and so has nothing to overlap. Q04 therefore does not strengthen the ASYNCHRONY argument; it strengthens IMP-002 (do not miss in the first place). Recorded explicitly so the Q04 relation is not misread as evidence for asynchrony.
Raw: Q04-cubrid-headline-telemetry-run2.json, profile-cubrid-callgraph.txt, q4-trace-cubrid.out.
improvements.mechanism_cubrid: pgbuf_fix_release() (page_buffer.c:2211) looks the page up; on a miss it calls fileio_read() (page_buffer.c:8464), which performs one pread of exactly one 16 KiB page (file_io.c:3935) on the calling query thread and blocks until the kernel has copied it. There is no asynchronous submission anywhere in the data path - the only aio_read in the tree is inside a pread() compatibility shim that immediately calls aio_suspend (file_io.c:3745-3767) - and no per-scan readahead hint, the single posix_fadvise being a mount-time whole-volume advise (file_io.c:3050). The multi-page primitive fileio_read_pages() (file_io.c:4211) exists but is wired only to the log paths. Consequently the page-cache copy and lookup cost appears as kernel time inside cub_server's query threads: at matched plan shape rep_movs_alternative 5.95%; in the native index-nested-loop plan rep_movs_alternative 13.83% plus filemap_get_read_batch 1.82%, filemap_read 0.98%, xas_load 0.74% and xas_descend 0.70%.
improvements.mechanism_postgresql: A sequential scan pulls buffers from a ReadStream (read_stream.c:1030), which looks ahead over the scan's block sequence and submits I/O through io_method=worker, so a separate io worker process (method_worker.c:482/687) performs the wait and the copy while the executor keeps processing buffers that are already available. Q03 measures 2.72 core-seconds of io worker CPU classified as auxiliary against only 0.78 core-seconds of kernel I/O inside the executor itself (next_uptodate_folio 2.48% + rep_movs_alternative 1.58% of 19.28 executor core-seconds). BAS_BULKREAD (freelist.c:442) separately confines a large scan to a small ring so it does not evict the rest of the pool - that effect belongs to IMP-002, not here.

improvements.priority_justification: Raised from P2 to P1 on Q06 evidence: 2.543 core-s and 11.01% of CUBRID's profiled self cost, 18.1% of Q06's CPU excess, with a call graph that resolves 100% of the sample weight to a synchronous single-page pread inside pgbuf_fix_release on the executor thread. On Q03/Q04 the asynchrony argument was weakened because PostgreSQL took few or zero physical reads; on Q06 both engines read, PostgreSQL reads 15.6x fewer times through vectored io-worker reads, and the difference is directly measurable. Still not P0 because IMP-010 removes 65% of the reads at a fraction of the implementation cost and should be done first, and because on this host no read reaches the device.

q06_evidence.call_graph: pgbuf_ordered_fix_release -> pgbuf_fix_release -> pgbuf_claim_bcb_for_fix -> fileio_read (src/storage/file_io.c:3935) -> __libc_pread64 -> __x64_sys_pread64 -> vfs_read -> xfs_file_read_iter -> xfs_file_buffered_read -> filemap_read -> copy_page_to_iter -> _copy_to_iter -> rep_movs_alternative. 100% of the 9.18% sample weight resolves to this one chain: the copy is on the executor thread, inside the buffer fix, one page at a time.
q06_evidence.contrast: CUBRID issues 15.6x the read syscalls and pays every one of them inside the executor; PostgreSQL batches misses into vectored reads (io_combine_limit = 16 pages) and executes them in separate pg_io_worker processes, so its executor profile contains NO kernel read-copy symbol at all and the cost appears as 0.34 core-s of auxiliary_query_cpu per statement instead of 2.543 core-s of executor CPU.
q06_evidence.multiplicative_note: MUST NOT be summed with IMP-010. IMP-010 governs how many misses occur (458,209 vs 158,930 pages); IMP-007 governs the per-miss cost. Their joint upper bound is the same 2.543 core-s band.
q06_evidence.summary: Q06 is IMP-007's largest measurement so far and its cleanest call-graph proof: the page-cache copy is sampled INSIDE pgbuf_fix_release on the query thread.

improvements.q08_relation: Q08 relation: 14,231 to 60,829 single-page preads per statement (block-dependent, see IMP-002), each exactly one 16 KiB CUBRID page - rchar/syscr = 16,344 bytes in every block. The synchronous nature shows up as 207,274 context switches in 20.002 s (2.734 K/s) against PostgreSQL's 7,880 (71/s), a 38.5x rate difference, and as 4.44% of CUBRID's profile in the page-cache read path (rep_movs_alternative 3.66% + filemap_get_read_batch 0.51% + filemap_read 0.27%). PostgreSQL issues 1,704 read syscalls per statement with read=0 at the buffer level. Q08 also reproduces the Q03/Q04/Q06 finding that cubrid statdump's global perfmon counters are frozen (delta 0 across a verified 4-statement block AND across a trivial serial count(*)), so all Q08 I/O evidence comes from /proc/<pid>/io.
improvements.q09_evidence: Q09: largest measured instance so far. 1,861,608 read syscalls per measured statement at 16,382 bytes each (= one 16 KiB data page per syscall), 30.497 GB/statement, read_bytes=0 so every one is a page-cache copy on the query thread. The kernel read path is 16.57% of CUBRID's profile (rep_movs_alternative 12.55%), i.e. 9.05 core-s of the 54.626 core-s statement. PostgreSQL, with io_method=worker, attributes 3.87 core-s/block to io workers as auxiliary CPU. raw/Q09/Q09-cubrid-buffer-io-diag.json, raw/Q09/profile-cubrid-flat.txt, raw/Q09/perf-stat-cubrid.txt.
improvements.q10_evidence: Q10: 10.36% of CUBRID's cycles are kernel page-cache copy on the query thread itself - rep_movs_alternative 8.07% whose call graph is _copy_to_iter <- copy_page_to_iter <- filemap_read <- xfs_file_buffered_read <- vfs_read <- __x64_sys_pread64 <- __libc_pread64 <- fileio_read <- pgbuf_claim_bcb_for_fix <- pgbuf_fix_release, plus filemap_get_read_batch 0.87%, iomap_set_range_uptodate 0.70%, filemap_read 0.41%, rwsem_optimistic_spin 0.31%. The statement issues 76,808 page ioreads (trace) and 560,637 read syscalls per statement (/proc/<cub_server>/io syscr delta 2,242,548 over the 4-statement block) for 9.18 GB of rchar per statement, with read_bytes = 0 - so every one of those preads is a page-cache hit whose copy cost is nonetheless paid synchronously inside the executor. PostgreSQL, with io_method=worker, shows 8.05% in kernel mm and only 0.78% in rep_movs_alternative on the profiled leader+worker set.

q_evidence.Q11: Q11 measures the cost of the reads IMP-018 removes, and is the cleanest such measurement in the campaign because the read count varies 566,103 -> 0 with everything else held constant. On the first connection the trace attributes 2,061 ms of a 3,360 ms statement to `fetch_time` and /proc/<cub_server>/io shows 551,116 read syscalls moving 8.406 GiB of rchar at exactly 16,384 bytes per syscall with device read_bytes delta 0 - i.e. 561,000 synchronous single-page preads served by the OS page cache on the query thread, at ~3.7 us each. In the saturated state fetch_time is 326 ms, the kernel page-cache-copy profile band is 0.00% (rep_movs_alternative below the 0.3% cut) and syscr is 96 per statement. So IMP-007's band on Q11 is 1,735 ms of 3,360 ms (51.6%) before IMP-018 and essentially nil after it. That ORDERS the two candidates: on Q11, removing the reads (IMP-018) dominates making them cheaper (IMP-007), and IMP-007's remaining Q11 value is zero. IMP-007 must be re-prioritised against what survives an IMP-018 fix.
q_evidence.Q12: Q12 adds a large synchronous-pread instance on a query where the miss COUNT is already bounded by IMP-010: 613,666 single-page 16 KiB preads per traced statement (722,946.5 per statement over the 4-statement diagnostic block), all issued on the six parallel-query threads themselves, moving 9.361-11.029 GiB through the page cache with device read_bytes 0. The cost is directly visible as profile band D: rep_movs_alternative 8.45% + filemap_get_read_batch 1.12% + filemap_read 0.65% = 10.22% = 2.4326 core-s of CUBRID's 23.8024 core-s. PostgreSQL's comparable band is 1.8966 core-s but is NOT the same mechanism and must not be read as one: with io_method=worker its reads are performed by separate io worker processes (telemetry auxiliary_query_cpu 8.41 core-s per block, correctly excluded from executor CPU) and its kernel band is dominated by mmap fault-in of the dynamic_shared_memory_type=mmap DSM segments (next_uptodate_folio 4.37%, filemap_map_pages 1.30%, folio_remove_rmap_ptes 1.43%) rather than by pread copy on the executor thread. That is exactly the critical-path-placement difference this candidate names, and Q12 is the cleanest example of it so far because both engines miss a comparable number of pages while only one pays for it inside the executor. raw/Q12/Q12-cubrid-buffer-io-diag.json, q12-profile-bands.txt, perf-stat-*.txt.
q_evidence.Q15: Q15 measures the syscall consequence directly, with device reads at ZERO on both engines so the entire cost is the synchronous single-page pread path itself and not disk. Per logical session CUBRID issues 1,161,523 read syscalls moving 18.14 GiB through read(), against PostgreSQL's 93,977 syscalls and 1.63 GiB - 12.4x and 11.1x. The kernel-side copy alone is 4.574 core-s per session (11.67% of CUBRID's profile), and its call graph names the mechanism exactly: rep_movs_alternative <- _copy_to_iter <- filemap_read <- __x64_sys_pread64 <- __libc_pread64 <- fileio_read <- pgbuf_claim_bcb_for_fix <- pgbuf_fix_release, i.e. the kernel copying one 16 KiB page at a time on the query thread. Together with IMP-002 this band is 10.504 core-s against PostgreSQL's 1.146, which is 9.358 of the 18.358 core-s total CPU gap (51%). Raw: q15-cubrid-io-{pre,mid,post}.txt, q15-postgresql-io-{pre,mid,post}.txt, profile-cubrid-callgraph.txt, q15-bands.txt. Evidence type: profile attribution.

improvements.ranking_rationale: Ranked third of the three Q03 candidates. Below IMP-006 on measured share of the matched-shape CPU excess (7.9% versus 18.7%) and below it on generality, since this only bites when the working set exceeds the buffer pool - true for Q03 (13.06 GiB against an 8 GiB pool) but not for Q02 (1.86 GiB). Above IMP-005 on runtime effect, which IMP-005 does not have at all. It was initially ranked P1 alongside IMP-006 on a read-combining argument; that argument was withdrawn when the syscall measurement showed CUBRID already moves more bytes per read call than PostgreSQL (17.2 versus 15.4 KiB), leaving only the critical-path placement effect, which is smaller and bounded. Its first implementation step is nevertheless the cheapest of the three candidates and has direct upstream precedent. Q04 demotes this relative to IMP-002: with PostgreSQL at zero physical reads there is no cross-engine asynchrony contrast on Q04, and the same 1.160 core-s is fully addressable by retention, so the marginal value of asynchrony on this query is bounded by what IMP-002 leaves behind, not added to it.

alternative: IMP-002 (reduce the NUMBER of misses via replacement policy) rather than the cost per miss; effects are NOT summed
relations.note: Complementary to IMP-002 and disjoint from IMP-006 by profile symbol. IMP-002 attacks how many pages must be re-read, IMP-007 attacks where the cost of each re-read is paid. Effects are not summed: part of the 1.68x byte difference against PostgreSQL belongs to IMP-002's retention deficit, not to this candidate.

improvements.root_cause_title: Every data-page buffer miss is served by a synchronous single-page pread on the query thread itself, with no asynchronous submission and no per-scan readahead, so page-cache copy and lookup cost is paid inside the executor's critical path instead of being overlapped by separate I/O processes
improvements.upstream_precedent: Yes for the readahead step: a05cfaa59 [CBRD-22319] 'add system parameter for read ahead fadvise' (#1282) introduced exactly the posix_fadvise machinery this candidate would extend from mount-time to per-scan, and it is an ancestor of the pinned build. No precedent for batching data-page reads through fileio_read_pages() (log-only to date) and none for asynchronous data-page I/O.
improvements.validation_criteria: (1) At matched plan shape, the kernel band charged to cub_server query threads falls below 3% of profiled self cost with unchanged bytes read, and controlled-plan median wall drops below 6.5 s with byte-identical output versus sink/Q03-cubrid-hash-block.out; (2) native Q03 median wall no worse than 4.808 s; (3) total_query_cpu does not increase - explicitly guarding against trading critical-path CPU for a larger total, which is the failure mode PostgreSQL's 0.432 core-seconds per GiB illustrates; (4) /proc syscr per statement recorded before and after so any submission-count claim is measured rather than assumed; (5) no change to any Q01-Q22 result; (6) double-write-buffer and page-validation paths exercised by the existing recovery tests.

improvements.correctness_risk: Medium. Comparison semantics - coercion rules, NULL handling, total versus ordinal order, collation for string domains - must be preserved exactly, and a wrongly cached domain decision silently changes predicate results rather than crashing. The constant-pre-coercion sub-step is materially lower risk because it changes WHEN a coercion happens, not WHICH one.

improvements.difficulty_reason: Localized to the predicate-evaluation entry points and the SCAN_PRED setup that already performs partial single-node-type specialization in eval_fnc(), so the hook exists; the work is in proving semantic equivalence across every domain pair rather than in restructuring the executor. The constant-pre-coercion sub-step alone is low difficulty.
improvements.effect_range: 0.825 core-s of the 4.558 core-s Q04 CPU excess (18.1%), as a profile-attribution difference against PostgreSQL's comparable band. Upper bound on CUBRID's side is the full 1.080 core-s band; a realistic target is the coercion and domain-resolution prologue, since the comparison itself is irreducible. No wall-clock claim is made: at 5.4 active units a CPU saving converts to wall only in proportion to utilization.
improvements.evidence_event: CPU-seconds in the predicate/expression-evaluation symbol band per statement; denominator = predicate evaluations, identical on both engines by construction: 15,000,000 orders rows x 2 date terms plus 832,820 lineitem rows x 1 date-vs-date term = 30,832,820 comparisons
improvements.explanation: Q04's filters are three plain date comparisons and both engines evaluate exactly the same number of them, yet CUBRID spends 1.080 core-s against PostgreSQL's 0.255 core-s - 4.24x - because CUBRID re-decides per row what it is comparing while PostgreSQL decided once at plan time.
improvements.implementation_direction: Specialize the sarg path at plan time instead of per row. eval_fnc() (query_evaluator.c:2590) already resolves a single-node type; extend that from choosing an evaluator FUNCTION to binding a resolved comparison for the concrete (domain, domain, REL_OP) triple, so eval_value_rel_cmp()'s per-call tp_domain_resolve_default()/tp_value_coerce() prologue at :178-262 runs once per scan rather than once per row. Cheapest first step: the constant side of a range sarg is known at compile time, so pre-coerce it to the column domain when the predicate is built and take the fast path unconditionally thereafter.

measurement.conservatism_note: PostgreSQL's ExecInterpExpr band is charged in FULL to predicates here even though the same interpreter also performs projection, which makes the 4.24x ratio conservative. CUBRID's fetch_val_list (0.55%) and mr_data_readval_date (0.42%) feed the same path and are deliberately EXCLUDED so this band cannot overlap IMP-006's materialization band.

q06_evidence.call_graph_proof: perf -g caller on the pinned binary: parallel_scan::slot_iterator::next_qualified_slot_with_peek -> eval_data_filter -> heap_attrinfo_read_dbvalues (17.89%) -> heap_attrvalue_read -> heap_attrvalue_transform_to_dbvalue -> mr_data_readval_numeric (8.40%) -> db_make_numeric (3.66%), and separately eval_data_filter -> eval_pred -> eval_pred -> eval_pred (nested PRED_EXPR walk, 6.36% at depth 3) -> eval_value_rel_cmp -> tp_value_compare_with_error -> tp_value_compare_with_error (recursive, 2.26%). Both chains are 100% attributable to the sarg path; nothing else calls them on this query.
q06_evidence.comparisons_note: 59,986,052 rows x 3 sarg terms (l_shipdate range = 2 comparisons folded into one range term, l_discount range, l_quantity <) as CUBRID's own plan dump counts them: term[0] range ge_lt, term[1] range ge_le, term[2] range inf_lt. PostgreSQL's Filter lists 5 scalar comparisons over the same 59,986,052 rows and removes 58,846,788 of them.
q06_evidence.new_finding: Q06 adds a component Q04 could not see, because Q04's sargs are dates and Q06's are NUMERIC: mr_data_readval_numeric alone is 8.72% = 2.014 core-s, decoding l_discount and l_quantity out of the record into a DB_VALUE through db_make_numeric on EVERY one of 59,986,052 rows, of which 58,846,788 are then discarded. PostgreSQL has NO counterpart symbol at all - a numeric Datum is a pointer into the page and cmp_numerics compares the on-disk digit arrays in place - so this is a structural absence, not a cost difference. It is the single largest structurally-absent band on CUBRID's side of Q06 after the kernel read path.
q06_evidence.plan_equality: F_plan = 1.0000 by structural equality and F_work = 1.0000 exactly (59,986,052 heap rows scanned on both engines), so the whole 2.4583x CPU factor is per-row cost with no plan or cardinality confound.
q06_evidence.plt_note: or_header_size@plt 1.07% and pr_type_from_id@plt 0.48% are pure PLT stub overhead inside this path: 1.55% = 0.358 core-s spent on cross-object indirect-call setup for per-row type dispatch, which a plan-time-resolved comparison would not perform at all.
q06_evidence.summary: Q06 is IMP-008's strongest evidence in the campaign and the query the candidate was written for: a bare three-sarg full scan where 54.4% of the entire CPU excess sits in this one root cause.

improvements.priority_justification: Raised from P1 to P0 on Q06 evidence. On Q04 this band was 0.825 core-s and 18.1% of that query's CPU excess, which justified P1. On Q06 - a bare three-sarg full scan with F_plan = 1.0000 and F_work = 1.0000, i.e. no plan or cardinality confound whatsoever - the same root cause accounts for 7.624 core-s and 54.4% of a 14.023 core-s CPU excess, and 4.23x on the directly comparable predicate band. It is now the largest single non-parallelism cost difference measured anywhere in this campaign, on a code path every sargable scan executes, and Q06 also supplies the missing A/B leverage the old P1 justification lacked: the NUMERIC decode component (2.014 core-s) is a structural absence in PostgreSQL rather than a dearer implementation of the same work, so at least that part is provably removable rather than irreducible.
improvements.q10_evidence: Q10: tp_value_compare_with_error 1.45% plus eval_pred 1.38%, eval_value_rel_cmp 0.56% and eval_data_filter 0.38% (3.77% banded) for two scan-level sargs - the o_orderdate range on the 15,000,000-row orders heap scan and l_returnflag='R' on the 2,292,924 lineitem index entries. PostgreSQL evaluates the same two predicates through compiled ExprEvalSteps: ExecInterpExpr 5.90% + bpchareq 5.13% on 59,986,052 lineitem and 15,000,000 orders rows, i.e. 26.1x the rows for 2.9x the relative cost.
improvements.q16_evidence: Q16 adds a fifth instance on a plan-controlled pair. Profile band D: CUBRID tp_value_compare_with_error 5.94% + eval_value_rel_cmp 3.98% + eval_pred 3.87% + mr_cmpval_int 0.74% + siblings = 16.75% of 9.4929 core-s = 1.5901 core-s per statement, against PostgreSQL's ExecInterpExpr 3.34% + ExecEvalScalarArrayOp 2.03% + FunctionCall2Coll 0.58% + bpcharne 0.50% + siblings = 7.34% of 3.67115 = 0.2695 core-s -- 5.90x. The predicate load is identical and independently counted on both sides: 2,000,000 part rows x three sargs (p_brand <>, p_type NOT LIKE, p_size IN with 8 values) plus 1,186,602 anti-join membership tests. tp_value_compare_with_error is Q16's single largest CUBRID symbol at 5.94%, ahead of every sort and every buffer symbol, which is this candidate's thesis in one line. Note the p_size IN list is where PostgreSQL's ExecEvalScalarArrayOp (2.03%) does in ONE specialised opcode what CUBRID reaches through eval_pred -> eval_pred_comp0 -> eval_value_rel_cmp -> tp_value_compare_with_error eight times.
improvements.q17_evidence: Q17 measures this on the campaign's cleanest denominator: a plan-shape-CONTROLLED cross-engine pair. PostgreSQL was forced into CUBRID's own plan shape with enable_hashjoin=off (the only change; query text untouched), so F_plan=8.9166x is anchored away on a same-engine A/B and the remaining pair -- CUBRID native 0.146000 s vs PostgreSQL-nlj 0.981877 s -- is structurally identical (part-driven index nested loop) AND takes zero physical reads on BOTH sides, removing residency as a confound. On that pair F_cpu=1.3667x (CPU_C 0.718958 vs CPU_Pc 0.982574 core-s) decomposes into F_work 0.535303x x F_cost 1.366905x, i.e. CUBRID reads 1.8681x FEWER executor tuples (2,122,770 vs 3,965,548) yet costs 1.3669x MORE per tuple read (338.69 ns vs 247.78 ns). Band C (scan-level predicate evaluation) is 19.59% of CUBRID's profile -> 0.14084 core-s: eval_pred 5.27% + mr_cmpval_char 4.51% + lang_fastcmp_byte 2.72% + tp_value_compare_with_error 2.69% + eval_value_rel_cmp 2.17% + eval_data_filter 1.84% + tp_value_cast_internal 0.39%. PostgreSQL's is 8.35% -> 0.08205 core-s: ExecInterpExpr 4.05% + bpchareq 2.08% + __memcmp_evex_movbe 1.35% + FunctionCall2Coll 0.44% + pg_newlocale_from_collation 0.43%. The denominator is exact and identical on both sides -- the SAME two bpchar equality sargs (p_brand='Brand#23', p_container='MED BOX') over the SAME 2,000,000 part rows, confirmed by CUBRID trace readrows 399,448..401,913 x 5 workers and by PostgreSQL 'Rows Removed by Filter: 1997956' + 2,044 output. Per part row: CUBRID 70.4 ns vs PostgreSQL 41.0 ns = 1.72x. Ranked SECOND of Q17's relations, behind IMP-020's 0.19779 core-s. Disjoint from IMP-020 (comparing a value vs materialising it); effects add but no core-second is claimed twice.

q_evidence.Q12: Q12 REFUTES this candidate's root cause as the deciding factor on this query while confirming its source set, and that refutation is why IMP-020 was allocated. Measured: CUBRID's comparator band (eval_pred 8.46% + tp_value_compare_with_error 5.07% + eval_value_rel_cmp 2.90% + eval_data_filter 1.63% + mr_cmpval_date 1.01% = 19.07% = 4.5391 core-s) is 0.913x of PostgreSQL's comparable compiled-expression band (bpchareq 12.47% + ExecEvalScalarArrayOp 7.91% + ExecInterpExpr 6.62% + pg_newlocale_from_collation 1.39% + ArrayGetNItemsSafe 0.80% = 29.19% = 4.9697 core-s) -- CUBRID is CHEAPER in absolute core-seconds, at 39.1 ns per term evaluation against PostgreSQL's 54.3 ns, while performing 1.1605x MORE evaluations (106,195,014 vs 91,506,768). On Q04 this band was 4.24x AGAINST CUBRID; the difference is the data type: Q04's comparisons are NUMERIC and DATE where the coercion prologue dominates, Q12's are DATE-vs-DATE and CHAR(10)-vs-constant where it does not. IMP-008's Q04/Q06/Q10 evidence and its P0 priority are unchanged, but its effect must not be assumed to generalize to every sarg-bound query: Q12 is a counter-example with a measured number. What Q12 DOES confirm is the materialisation half of IMP-008's cited source set (heap_file.c:10464, the mr_data_readval_* readers), now tracked as IMP-020 with a 4.7073 core-s delta. raw/Q12/q12-profile-bands.txt, q12-selectivity-probe-*.out.
q_evidence.Q15: Q15 is this candidate's cleanest isolation so far: the l_shipdate range is the ONLY qual, applied to 119,972,104 lineitem rows per session (2 x 59,986,052, one per revenue0 expansion) with identical row counts on both engines and an essentially exact selectivity estimate on both sides (CUBRID sel 0.0380283 -> 2,281,165 estimated against 2,265,714 actual, +0.68%), so no estimation error is mixed into the number. CUBRID spends 5.957 core-s per session in eval_pred (6.88%) + tp_value_compare_with_error (4.11%) + eval_value_rel_cmp (2.44%) + eval_data_filter (1.77%) = 15.20% of its profile; PostgreSQL spends 2.434 core-s in ExecInterpExpr (8.18%) + ExecSeqScanWithQual (2.74%) + make_result_safe (0.76%) = 11.68%. Ratio 2.45x on the identical predicate and the identical rows, contributing 3.524 core-s (19%) of the 18.358 core-s gap. Raw: profile-cubrid-flat-nocg.txt, profile-pg-flat-nocg.txt, q15-bands.txt. Evidence type: profile attribution.

improvements.ranking_rationale: Ranked immediately below IMP-002 on Q04 (18.1% vs 25.5% of the CPU excess) and above IMP-007, whose Q04 asynchrony argument does not apply because PostgreSQL takes zero physical reads. Bands are verified disjoint by symbol: IMP-002 and IMP-007 are kernel copy plus buffer manager, IMP-008 is predicate evaluation, IMP-006 is intermediate-tuple materialization (small on Q04 - fetch_val_list 0.55% - because this plan materializes only 526,040 result tuples). The bands are NOT summed.

improvements.root_cause_title: Scan-level sarg evaluation routes every row through the generic DB_VALUE comparator tp_value_compare_with_error(), with per-call domain resolution and coercion, where PostgreSQL compiles the qual once into type-specialized ExprEvalSteps and calls the resolved datum comparison directly

WALL effect is near zero because the five copies run concurrently, so this is a CPU-efficiency item on Q16, not a latency item -- stated explicitly so it is not double-counted against IMP-023's serial-phase band. q_evidence.Q11: Q11 is a DIRECT structural instance and the second-largest measured Q11 factor after IMP-018. Q11's `having sum(...) > (select sum(...) from partsupp, supplier, nation where ...)` is an uncorrelated subquery that repeats the main query's whole join, and CUBRID's saturated trace shows it as `SUBQUERY (uncorrelated) -> SELECT (time: 619, fetch: 340131, ioread: 0)` with NO `parallel workers` sub-line - 619 ms of a 1,532 ms statement (40.4%) executed on one thread. PostgreSQL runs the identical subquery as `InitPlan expr_1 -> Finalize Aggregate -> Gather (Workers Planned: 1, Workers Launched: 1) -> Partial Aggregate` and completes it in 237 ms. That single worker is worth a measured 1.091149x to PostgreSQL: forcing max_parallel_workers_per_gather=0 moves PostgreSQL from 0.798124 s to 0.870872 s with U falling 1.24996 -> 0.98764. It is also the whole of Q11's F_units 1.238013x, because it is PostgreSQL's ONLY parallel unit. So Q11 supplies a controlled cross-engine measurement of what compute_parallel_degree()'s `case parallel_type::SUBQUERY` degree-1 hardcode costs: on equal (serial) units CUBRID loses 1.540984x rather than 1.681443x. This is a PROJECTION for the CUBRID side (the A/B was executed on PostgreSQL), not a CUBRID A/B; IMP-009's direct CUBRID A/B remains Q05's.

improvements.correctness_risk: Low for the insertion-point variants: LRU placement is a performance policy and cannot change query results, and the buffer's own latching/pinning is untouched. The real risks are operational rather than semantic: (a) sharing one private LRU list across N workers concentrates list-mutation traffic on one lock, so it must be measured for contention at high DOP, and the fallback variant above exists for exactly that outcome; (b) a private list that now legitimately holds the whole pool must not starve other sessions, so pgbuf_adjust_quotas' behaviour under a single large private consumer needs checking - note that the SERIAL path already produces exactly this state today, so it is a state the pool demonstrably tolerates.
